findings.title: Race condition in match_count increment
findings.body: should_block? reads the record then increments match_count and saves without locking or atomic update. Under concurrent requests for the same blocked email, increments can be lost due to read-modify-write races (two requests load the same match_count, both increment and save, one update is overwritten). Should use update_all/increment! with SQL-level atomicity.

findings.title: BlockedEmail check only runs when email changes, but every create changes email
findings.body: This is mostly fine for new users, but on existing user update() flows where email doesn't change, the email: true validator (and BlockedEmail.should_block?) won't run — that's expected. However the bigger issue is validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed? combined with EmailValidator calling BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) means every save that changes email (e.g. change_email flow in users_controller) will increment match_count/last_match_at on the BlockedEmail table even for validation-only checks that may be re-run multiple times per request (e.g. due to uniqueness validation combined with email validation both triggering saves on the user, or multiple validate! calls), causing inflated match_count statistics not reflecting actual distinct block attempts.

findings.title: should_block? mutates state as a side effect of a query-named method
findings.body: should_block? looks like a predicate/query method but has side effects (increments match_count, updates last_match_at, saves to DB) on every call. This violates the principle of least surprise: validations or other code paths calling should_block? multiple times (e.g. validated twice during a single form submission, or re-validated via valid? before save in users_controller#create) will record multiple matches for a single actual attempt, corrupting match statistics. Also no error handling if save fails silently (return value of save ignored).

findings.title: Full error hash and submitted attribute values exposed to client on failed signup
findings.body: The create action now returns errors: user.errors.to_hash and values: user.attributes.slice("name","username","email") in the JSON response. While limited to name/username/email, returning raw error hashes could leak additional validation messages (e.g., any new validator added later) not intended for display, and echoes back the submitted email, which combined with the blocked email check could allow an attacker to probe which emails are in the blocked list by observing error type (not_allowed vs blocked) in response text — enumerating blocklist membership.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline / file-level validator not covering nil values
findings.body: value could be nil if email is nil; email_in_restriction_setting? and BlockedEmail.should_block? call regexp/match on nil, which could raise NoMethodError for a blank email during validation, instead of simply skipping (presence validator should catch this, but order of validators execution isn't guaranteed, so a nil email could raise an unhandled error here).
